title: Catching up
goal: Catch up with a friend: ask what's new, share news (graduated, got married, moved abroad), say what you were doing when something happened, ask 'have you ever …?', and say how long ago or since when.
intro:
When Pashtuns meet after a while, there is a whole ritual of questions — how are you, how's the family, what's new — and then the real catching up starts: who got married, who's working abroad, who finally passed their driving test. To join in you need to talk about the past in three different ways.

In this unit you'll learn the **present perfect** for news and experiences ('he **has** got married', '**have** you ever been to Kandahar?') and how it differs from the simple past, the **past continuous** for what you **were doing** ('I was at work when you called'), and how to say **ago**, **since** and **for** — including the very Pashto 'it's been two years that …'.

grammar.title: 'I did' or 'I have done'? Past vs present perfect
grammar.body:
You met both forms in unit 16. In conversation the difference matters:

**Simple past** (perfective): a finished event, often with a time: پرون مې احمد **وليد** 'I saw Ahmad yesterday'; تېر کال يې واده **وکړ** 'he got married last year'.

**Present perfect** = past participle + present of 'be'. Use it for:
• **news** whose result matters now: احمد واده **کړی دی** 'Ahmad has got married'; زلمي ته زوی پيدا **شوی دی** 'Zalmay has had a baby boy'
• **change**: ډېر بدل **شوی يې** 'you've changed a lot'
• **experience — 'have you ever …?'**, with **کله** 'ever' and **هېڅکله** 'never': ته کله کندهار ته **تللی يې**؟ — هو، يو ځل / نه، هېڅکله نه يم تللی

**Participle endings**: **-ay** (m sg) · **-i** (m pl) · **-e** (f sg and pl): تللی، تللي، تللې · ليدلی، ليدلي، ليدلې · شوی، شوي، شوې · کړی، کړي، کړې.

**Who does it agree with?** Intransitive verbs agree with the subject: زه تللی **يم** (man), زه تللې **يم** (woman). Transitive verbs are **ergative**: the doer is ما / تا / a clitic, and both the participle and 'be' agree with the **object**: ما کابل ليدلی **دی** (m); ما ستا مور ليدل**ې** **ده** (f).

**Negative**: نه goes before the 'be' verb, which then comes before the participle: ما دا فلم **نه دی ليدلی**; زه هېڅکله **نه يم تللی**.

In fast speech the 'be' verb is often dropped: احمد واده کړی! 'Ahmad's got married!'

grammar.title: 'I was doing': the past continuous
grammar.body:
To say what was **going on** when something else happened, Pashto uses the **imperfective past**: the ordinary stem (no **و-**) with the past endings, stressed on the ending. The perfective past (with و-, stressed at the front) is for the event that **interrupted** it:

زه بازار ته **تلم** چې ته مې **وليدې** 'I was going to the bazaar when I saw you'

Intransitive verbs take the subject's endings: تلم، تلې، ته (m) / تله (f)، تلو، تلئ، تلل. Being in a state just uses the past of 'be': ويده **وم** 'I was asleep', ويښ **وو** 'we were awake', روان **وم** 'I was on my way'.

Transitive verbs are **ergative** here too — the verb agrees with the object: ما فلم **کاته** 'I was watching a film' (فلم m), ما ډوډۍ **خوړله** 'I was eating' (f). With no object, use the masculine plural: څه دې **کول**؟ 'what were you doing?'.

**The easy way out**: **په** + infinitive in **-o** + **لګيا وم** 'I was busy …-ing' works with every verb and dodges the ergative: **په ډوډۍ پخولو لګيا وم** 'I was (busy) cooking', **په کار لګيا وم** 'I was busy working'.

Join the two events with **کله چې** 'when' at the front, or with **چې** after the continuous part: کور ته روان وم **چې** باران شروع شو 'I was on my way home when it started raining'.

examples.en: I was watching a film when the power went.

examples.en: When you came, I was asleep.

examples.en: We were on our way home when Ahmad called.

grammar.title: Ago, since and for
grammar.body:
**Ago** = time + **مخکې** (or وړاندې): دوه کاله **مخکې** 'two years ago', لس دقيقې مخکې 'ten minutes ago'.

**Since** = **له** … **راهيسې** (or د … راهيسې): **له** پرون **راهيسې** 'since yesterday', له ماشومتوبه راهيسې 'since childhood', **له کله راهيسې**؟ 'since when?'.

**For (up to now)**: English says 'I **have been** living here for two years'; Pashto uses the **present** with **د … راهيسې**: د دوو کالو راهيسې دلته **اوسېږم**. Or, very commonly, **'it's been X that …'** with **کېږي**:
دوه کاله **کېږي چې** دلته اوسېږم 'I've been living here for two years'
يو کال **کېږي چې** هغه مې نه دی ليدلی 'I haven't seen him for a year'
څو کاله کېږي چې …؟ 'how long have you been …?'

**For (finished)**: for a period that is over, just put the time in front, with no postposition: دوه کاله مې هلته کار **وکړ** 'I worked there for two years'.

**The trap**: don't use the past tense with راهيسې for something still going on — له پرون راهيسې تبه **لرم** 'I've had a fever since yesterday' (present: I still have it).

dialogue.title: Long time no see
dialogue.setting: Sami is buying bread on University Road in Peshawar when he spots an old classmate, Naveed.

lines.speaker: Sami

lines.roman: guzārá kéẓi. la pohantún na fārə́ġ shwəm, os pə yawa bānk ke kār kawə́m.
lines.en: Getting by. I graduated, and now I work at a bank.

lines.speaker: Sami

lines.roman: ho, ter kāl me wādə́ wə́kaṛ. yáwa lur ham lárəm!

lines.speaker: Naveed

lines.speaker: Sami

lines.roman: də mermə́ne paxláy day! … os chérta rawā́n we?
lines.en: That's my wife's cooking! … So where were you off to just now?

lines.speaker: Naveed
lines.native: بازار ته تلم چې ته مې وليدې.
lines.roman: bāzā́r ta tləm che tə me wə́lide.
lines.en: I was on my way to the bazaar when I saw you.

lines.speaker: Sami
lines.native: پرېږده بازار! راځه چای وڅښو، ډېرې خبرې لرو.
lines.roman: préẓda bāzā́r! rā́dza chāy wə́tsṣu, ḍére xabə́re láru.
lines.en: Forget the bazaar! Come on, let's have tea — we've got loads to talk about.

lines.native: ښه، خو چای ستا په غاړه!
lines.roman: ṣə, xo chāy stā pə ġā́ṛa!
lines.en: OK, but the tea's on you!

culture: A Pashtun greeting between friends who haven't met for a while is a rapid-fire string of questions, often asked by both people at once without waiting for answers: **ستړی مه شې، جوړ يې، ښه يې، خوشحاله يې، کور کهول ښه دي، ماشومان ښه دي؟** — the answer to all of them is **شکر** or **ښه يم، ته څنګه يې؟**. Only then does the real catching up begin. Personal questions that might feel nosy in English — are you married yet? how many children? how much do you earn? — are normal signs of interest, and **چاغ شوی يې** 'you've put on weight' is said cheerfully (to an older generation it meant you're doing well). **مسافر** has a special meaning: hundreds of thousands of Pashtun men work in the Gulf, Malaysia or Europe, and 'he's مسافر' means he's away earning for the family; coming home from مسافري is a big event. The weekend is Friday (Thursday afternoon too) in Afghanistan and Sunday in Pakistan, so ask accordingly.

lessons.title: Have you ever …?

tip.title: 'Have you ever …?': the perfect
tip.body:
- Participle (**-ay** m · **-i** m pl · **-e** f) + 'be': ته کله … **تللی يې**؟
- **کله** = ever, **هېڅکله** = never, **يو ځل** = once.
- Transitive: ergative, agrees with the object: تا کله زما مور **ليدلې ده**؟
- Negative: **نه** + 'be' + participle: نه يم تللی، نه دی ليدلی.

lessons.title: What were you doing?

tip.title: 'I was doing': imperfective past
tip.body:
- No **و-**, stress on the ending: زه بازار ته **تلم** 'I was going'.
- States: ويده **وم**، ويښ **وو**، روان **وم**.
- Transitive: ergative: ما فلم **کاته**; no object: څه دې **کول**؟
- Easy option: **په** … **-و لګيا وم**: په کار لګيا وم 'I was busy working'.

new: کله چې تا زنګ ووهه، زه په کار لګيا وم.

sentences.native: پرون چې ما زنګ درته واهه، څه دې کول؟
sentences.roman: parún che mā zang dərta wāhə́, tsə de kawə́l?
sentences.en: Yesterday when I kept calling you, what were you doing?

sentences.native: په ډوډۍ پخولو لګيا وم.
sentences.roman: pə ḍoḍə́y paxawə́lo lagyā́ wəm.
sentences.en: I was busy cooking.

sentences.native: ما فلم کاته، ټيلفون مې بل ځای و.
sentences.roman: mā film kātə́, ṭelifún me bəl dzāy wə.
sentences.en: I was watching a film; my phone was somewhere else.

sentences.native: تر نيمې شپې ويښ وم.
sentences.roman: tər níme shpe wiṣ wəm.
sentences.en: I was up till midnight.

sentences.native: ولې تر نيمې شپې ويښ وې؟
sentences.roman: wə́le tər níme shpe wiṣ we?
sentences.en: Why were you up till midnight?

sentences.native: ټوله ورځ په کار لګيا وو.
sentences.roman: ṭóla wradz pə kār lagyā́ wu.
sentences.en: We were busy working all day.

sentences.native: کله چې مې وليدې، جيم ته تلم.
sentences.roman: kə́la che me wə́lide, jim ta tləm.
sentences.en: When I saw you, I was on my way to the gym.

sentences.native: زه کور ته روان وم چې باران شروع شو.
sentences.roman: zə kor ta rawā́n wəm che bārā́n shurúʿ shu.
sentences.en: I was on my way home when it started to rain.

sentences.native: کله چې ته راغلې، زه لا ويده وم.
sentences.roman: kə́la che tə rā́ġle, zə lā widə́ wəm.
sentences.en: When you came, I was still asleep.

sentences.native: ته اوس هم جيم ته ځې؟
sentences.roman: tə os ham jim ta dze?
sentences.en: Do you still go to the gym?

sentences.native: جمعه مې په کور کې تېره کړه، هېڅ مې ونه کړل.
sentences.roman: jumʿá me pə kor ke téra kṛa, hets me wə́na kṛəl.
sentences.en: I spent Friday at home and didn't do a thing.

lessons.title: How long? Since when?

tip.title: Ago, since, for
tip.body:
- Ago: time + **مخکې**: لس ورځې مخکې.
- Since: **له** … **راهيسې**: له پرون راهيسې.
- For (still going): **present** + د … راهيسې, or **X کېږي چې** …: دوه کاله کېږي چې دلته اوسېږم.
- For (finished): no postposition: دوه کاله مې هلته کار وکړ.
tip.pattern: له … راهيسې · X مخکې · X کېږي چې …

new: څو کاله کېږي چې دلته اوسېږې؟

sentences.native: له پرون راهيسې تبه لرم.
sentences.roman: la parún rāhíse tabə́ lárəm.
sentences.en: I've had a fever since yesterday.

sentences.native: د دوو کالو راهيسې دلته کار کوم.
sentences.roman: də dwo kā́lo rāhíse dálta kār kawə́m.
sentences.en: I've been working here for two years.

sentences.native: لس ورځې مخکې کابل ته لاړم.
sentences.roman: las wradzé mə́xke kābúl ta lā́ṛəm.
sentences.en: I went to Kabul ten days ago.

sentences.native: يو کال کېږي چې هغه مې نه دی ليدلی.
sentences.roman: yaw kāl kéẓi che haġá me na day lidə́lay.
sentences.en: I haven't seen him for a year.

sentences.native: تقريباً دوه ساعته کېږي چې ستا انتظار کوم!
sentences.roman: taqribán dwa sāʿáta kéẓi che stā intizā́r kawə́m!
sentences.en: I've been waiting for you for nearly two hours!

sentences.native: له کله راهيسې په کابل کې يې؟
sentences.roman: la kə́la rāhíse pə kābúl ke ye?
sentences.en: Since when have you been in Kabul?

sentences.native: له ماشومتوبه راهيسې سره ملګري يو.
sentences.roman: la māshumtobá rāhíse sara malgə́ri yu.
sentences.en: We've been friends since we were kids.

sentences.native: تقريباً پنځه کاله مخکې مو واده وکړ.
sentences.roman: taqribán pindzə́ kā́la mə́xke mo wādə́ wə́kaṛ.
sentences.en: We got married about five years ago.

sentences.native: د مور پخلی مې ډېر ياد شوی دی.
sentences.roman: də mor paxláy me ḍer yād shə́way day.
sentences.en: I've really missed my mum's cooking.

sentences.native: دوه کاله مې هلته کار وکړ.
sentences.roman: dwa kā́la me hálta kār wə́kaṛ.
sentences.en: I worked there for two years.

sentences.native: زما اوسنی کار تر پخواني ښه دی.
sentences.roman: zmā osanáy kār tər pəxwāní ṣə day.
sentences.en: My current job is better than my old one.
